spec_match.rationale: Covers all five counter-style systems from CSS Counter Styles 3 side by side, including the positional two-symbol validity rule and fixed's decimal fallback framing.

interactive.rationale: Symbols input and list-length slider re-render all five cards live with per-card validity states; verified dropping to one symbol flips numeric/alphabetic to 'needs at least 2 symbols; 1 given'.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises same-symbols-five-systems separation as the list outgrows the symbol set, which is exactly the page's overflow-note framing.

edge_cases.rationale: Empty symbol input, one-symbol positional invalidity, list-shorter-than-set, and full browser unsupport each get a distinct, honest state.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146996093616128 and the symbols() function section of the spec.

conformance.rationale: The suite's all-five-systems and positional-two-symbol assertions are this page's exact subject; /conformance/ honestly reported 1 pass / 7 fail on Chromium 141 because symbols() needs Chrome 154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): exercised both controls, per-card states read 'not supported in this browser' with the amber banner shown, console clean, no failed same-origin requests, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a systems-rendered assert with symbols/items/valid/supported on each render.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, rose-bordered unsupported cards, amber support banner, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled text input and range with live value span, aria-live output, per-card state conveyed as text rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); the card grid collapses to one column.

openQuestions.title: Simulate the five systems' output when symbols() is unavailable
openQuestions.detail: On any pre-154 Chromium the page's whole lesson — how cyclic, symbolic, numeric, alphabetic and fixed diverge past the symbol count — is invisible: every card shows default decimal markers and only the prose describes the difference. All five algorithms are trivially computable in JS (the spec defines them constructively), so when CSS.supports fails the cards could render a clearly-labelled simulated marker column ('simulated — CSS symbols() needs Chrome 154') next to each item. That keeps the fallback honest while preserving the demo's teaching value for the majority of visitors on older builds.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/css-symbols/system-explorer/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp), where symbols() is genuinely unsupported. Fallback handling is exemplary — amber banner, per-card 'not supported in this browser' states, validity rules still evaluated and narrated (one-symbol input correctly invalidates only the positional systems) — and both controls re-render live with clean console/network (font-CDN cert failure is a sandbox artifact). Desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read without overflow; /conformance/ honestly reported 1 pass / 7 fail on this build. The one substantive improvement is a labelled JS simulation of the five systems so the comparison is visible before Chrome 154.
